syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: The Summer of the Beautiful White Horse

topics.title: Mourad arrives with the white horse: poverty and the family's honesty

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how the story opens, with Mourad waking nine-year-old Aram at dawn on a white horse.
Explain why the family's poverty and famous honesty made Aram doubt what he saw.
Analyse how Aram persuades himself that riding the horse is not stealing.

topics.title: The dawn ride and the crazy streak in the tribe

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Mourad as the natural descendant of the crazy streak in the Garoghlanian tribe.
Explain what Uncle Khosrove's behaviour and refrain reveal about his character.
Interpret the idea that a father of the flesh need not be the father of the spirit.

topics.title: Aram's turn to ride and hiding the horse

concepts.learning_objective: Recall what happened when Aram tried to ride the horse alone.
Explain where and why the boys hid the horse and what Mourad told Aram to say.
Evaluate Mourad's claim of a simple and honest understanding with horses.

topics.title: John Byro's visit and Mourad's promise

concepts.learning_objective: Describe John Byro and the loss of his horse as told at Aram's house.
Explain Uncle Khosrove's outburst and the mother's explanation of it.
Interpret Mourad's reaction to keeping the horse and the episode of the robin.

topics.title: The meeting with John Byro and the return of the horse

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how John Byro's faith in the family's honesty shapes the meeting on the road.
Recall how the horse was returned and how John Byro found it.

topics.title: Theme, narration and humour

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the author, narrator and nostalgic first-person narration of the story.
Evaluate whether the boys returned the horse out of conscience or out of fear.
Explain how the story draws its interest from humour, irony and character rather than action.

topics.title: The first visit to Number 46

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Mrs Dorling's cold, evasive reception of the narrator on her first visit.
Explain how the green knitted cardigan confirms the narrator's identification of the woman.

topics.title: The mother and Mrs Dorling during the War
topics.ncert_sections: Flashback: the first half of the War

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how Mrs Dorling carried away the family's possessions and the reason she gave.
Contrast the mother's trust in Mrs Dorling with the narrator's doubt.

topics.title: Fear of memories and the return of normal life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the narrator delayed going to the address after the Liberation.
Interpret the images that show life slowly becoming normal and reviving the narrator's curiosity.

topics.title: The second visit: familiar things in a strange room

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the objects the narrator recognises in Mrs Dorling's living-room and the memories they carry.
Interpret the episode of the silver cutlery and the girl's ignorance of its worth.

topics.title: The decision to forget and the story's theme

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the narrator resolves to forget the address and leave the objects behind.
Evaluate the story as an account of the human predicament that follows war.

topics.title: The setting and the neighbours' conversation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the setting, time and principal characters of the play.
Explain Mrs Fitzgerald's advice that Mrs Pearson should assert herself in her own home.

topics.title: The magical exchange of personalities

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how and why the two women exchange personalities.
Interpret the stage directions that contrast the two women's voices and manners.

topics.title: Mrs Pearson confronts Doris and Cyril

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse how the transformed Mrs Pearson deals with Doris's demands.
Explain Mrs Pearson's argument about the forty-hour week and trade-union methods.

topics.title: George Pearson and the club

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse George's character and his reaction to the truth about the club.
Evaluate how Mrs Pearson insists on decent manners towards a neighbour.

topics.title: Changing back and the resolution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the women change back and what Mrs Fitzgerald advises afterwards.
Interpret the final scene and the changed behaviour of the family.

topics.title: Themes, humour and satire

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the play's satirical portrayal of the status of the mother in a family.
Analyse how fantasy, humour and dramatic devices convey the play's social message.

topics.title: The night call to Blaina Terrace

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the setting, the characters and the situation that open the story.
Interpret Joe Morgan's anxiety and trust as he brings Andrew to his wife.

topics.title: Waiting through the night

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse Andrew's troubled thoughts about marriage and his decision to stay.
Explain the hopes and fears of Susan Morgan and her mother about the child.

topics.title: The delivery and Andrew's dilemma

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse the dilemma Andrew faces when the child is born lifeless.
Describe how Andrew saves the collapsing mother first.

topics.title: Bringing the stillborn child to life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Andrew recognises asphyxia pallida and the method he uses.
Evaluate the role of Andrew's persistence in the child's revival.

topics.title: Something real at last: meaning and language

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the meaning of Andrew's realisation at the end of the story.
Evaluate the difference between textbook medicine and real practice.
Interpret the vocabulary, similes and imagery used in the story.

topics.title: The King's arch and the lost crown

concepts.learning_objective: Recall why the King ordered the arch and how its low height cost him his crown.
Explain the irony in the poet calling the King 'just and placid'.

topics.title: The chain of blame

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how the blame passed from the chief of builders to the workmen, masons and architect.
Evaluate the King's hasty and literal idea of justice in ordering hangings.

topics.title: The wise man's verdict and the King's hanging

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the wisest man's verdict that the arch itself must be hanged.
Analyse how the restless crowd led the King to want any hanging and how he was hanged by his own decree.

topics.title: The Melon becomes King

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the custom by which the ministers chose the next ruler at the City Gate.
Explain the people's attitude to the Melon King and the meaning of laissez faire.

topics.title: Humour, irony and form of the poem

concepts.learning_objective: Identify instances of humour and irony that satirise rulers and the state.
Identify the poet, source and narrative verse form of the poem, including its rhyming couplets.
